question: How does % of patients meeting weekly exercise goal change across 4 follow up visits for home and center based rehab?
audience: The cardiac rehab program coordinator who can use the results to identify where additional follow up support may be helpful
intended_claim: Both programs demonstrate increase in goal achievement across visits. Center based patients have higher percentage of visits
y_measure: % of patients seen who met weekly goal of 150 minutes of exercise
grain: Each row and plotted point represents one rehabilitation program at one follow up visit
text_alternative: This line chart compares the percentage of patients meeting the weekly exercise goal of 150 minutes across four follow-up visits for home-based and center-based rehan programs. The x-axis represents follow-up visits from 1 to 4, while the y-axis represents the percentage meeting the exercise goal. Both programs show an increasing trend, with home-based patients improving from 58% to 70% and center-based patients improving from 57% to 79%. At visit 4, center-based patients had a 9-percentage-point higher rate. However, patients selected their own programs, so these differences do not establish causation. The percentages also include only patients seen at each visit, and random variation or differences in who returned could influence the results.
